* **Mentora is a keyboard-first desktop application for managing student and guardian contacts at small private tuition centres in Singapore.**
* It is designed for coordinators who manage approximately 30-200 active and prospective secondary-school students.

* It helps coordinators keep related student and guardian information together, retrieve the right contacts quickly, and maintain accurate enrolment-related records without relying on cumbersome spreadsheets or mouse-heavy systems.
* adding, updating, viewing, searching, and deleting student records;
* linking a student to one guardian while allowing siblings to share the same guardian record;
* browsing five configured subject or class groups and assigning them to students;
* displaying a student's academic level, assignments, and linked guardian; and
* saving records locally, restoring them when the application is reopened, and protecting an unreadable data file from being overwritten.
* Mentora is optimized for **fast typed commands** and clear feedback, while retaining a graphical interface for viewing student profiles and contact information.

* The MVP is intended for one coordinator using the application locally at a time. It does not manage attendance, grades, fees, payroll, accounting, lesson content, or direct messaging through WhatsApp, SMS, or email.
* This project is based on the AddressBook-Level3 project created by the [SE-EDU initiative](https://se-education.org)

The following provides a quick overview of the main components and their interactions.

**`Main`** (consisting of classes [`Main`](https://github.com/se-edu/addressbook-level3/tree/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/Main.java) and [`MainApp`](https://github.com/se-edu/addressbook-level3/tree/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/MainApp.java)) is in charge of the app launch and shut down.
* At app launch, it initializes the other components in the correct sequence, and connects them up with each other.
* At shut down, it shuts down the other components and invokes cleanup methods where necessary.
The bulk of the app's work is done by the following four components:
* [**`Model`**](#model-component): Holds the data of the App in memory.
* [**`Storage`**](#storage-component): Reads data from, and writes data to, the hard disk.
[**`Commons`**](#common-classes) represents a collection of classes used by multiple other components.
**How the architecture components interact with each other**
The *Sequence Diagram* below shows how the components interact with each other for the scenario where the user issues the command `delete 1`.
Each of the four main components (also shown in the diagram above),
* defines its *API* in an `interface` with the same name as the Component.
* provides its functionality through a concrete `{Component Name}Manager` class that implements the corresponding API interface.

For example, the `Logic` component defines its API in `Logic.java` and implements it in `LogicManager.java`. Other components interact with a component through its interface rather than its concrete class, preventing them from coupling to that component's implementation, as illustrated in the following partial class diagram.
The sections below give more details of each component.
The **API** of this component is specified in [`Ui.java`](https://github.com/se-edu/addressbook-level3/tree/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/ui/Ui.java)

The UI consists of a `MainWindow` and its parts, such as `CommandBox`, `ResultDisplay`, `PersonListPanel`, and `StatusBarFooter`. All of these, including `MainWindow`, inherit from the abstract `UiPart` class, which captures common behavior among classes that represent visible GUI parts.

The `UI` component uses the JavaFX UI framework. The layouts of these UI parts are defined in matching `.fxml` files in `src/main/resources/view`. For example, [`MainWindow.fxml`](https://github.com/se-edu/addressbook-level3/tree/master/src/main/resources/view/MainWindow.fxml) specifies the layout of [`MainWindow`](https://github.com/se-edu/addressbook-level3/tree/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/ui/MainWindow.java).
* executes user commands using the `Logic` component.
* listens for changes to `Model` data so that the UI can be updated with the modified data.
* keeps a reference to the `Logic` component, because the `UI` relies on the `Logic` to execute commands.
* depends on some classes in the `Model` component because it displays `Person` objects from the model.

For these group commands, the execution path is:
1. `LogicManager.execute` passes the input to `AddressBookParser.parseCommand`. The router selects the concrete
parser, which validates the arguments and creates the corresponding `Command` subclass. The group parsers
retain the student ID as text and canonicalize the group code without allocating a `StudentId`.
1. Before executing a mutating command, `LogicManager` checks the storage recovery state and snapshots the
complete in-memory register. `Command.isReadOnly()` defaults to `false`; both group commands inherit that
classification. Read-only commands bypass saving, while recovery blocks mutations before execution.
1. The command executes against `Model`, resolving the student from the full register and the group from the
configured catalogue. It calls `addGroupAssignment` or `removeGroupAssignment`; domain validation and
mutation remain in the model. The command does not write to Storage or control the UI.
1. If execution changes the register, `LogicManager` saves it once through `Storage` before returning success.
Parsing and domain rejections, read-only commands and unchanged data do not trigger a save. A save
`IOException` restores the complete in-memory snapshot and becomes command-specific error feedback.
Normal file writes are not atomic, so this rollback does not guarantee preservation of partially written disk data.
1. After execution and any required save succeed, Logic reveals a requested student hidden by the current filter
and returns the `CommandResult`. The result carries feedback and optional student-ID selection and workspace
requests. The UI applies these requests and refreshes the profile; `CommandResult` performs no UI actions.
`add-group` and `delete-group` use the same router, recovery guard, snapshot and save boundary. Their parsers validate
group-specific prefixes and construct canonical `Group`/`GroupCode` values without touching student IDs. The commands
call `Model.addGroup` or `Model.deleteGroup`; `AddressBook` enforces code uniqueness and the no-assigned-students deletion
rule. `CommandResult` can request a canonical group-code selection, which `MainWindow` applies only after saving succeeds.

`ModelManager` implements the `Model` API and owns the in-memory `AddressBook` and user preferences. `AddressBook` is the complete register: it owns Student and Guardian records, the ordered group catalogue, student-to-guardian links and group assignments. It implements `ReadOnlyAddressBook` for callers that need to inspect the register without mutating it.

Students and Guardians are immutable records composed from their stable IDs and validated value types. A student may link to at most one guardian, while a guardian may be shared by multiple students. `AddressBook` stores these links by `StudentId` and `GuardianId`, so contact details stay on the Guardian record and are resolved when a profile is displayed.
`GroupAssignment` pairs a `StudentId` with a configured `GroupCode`. `AddressBook` validates that the student exists,
the group is configured, and the pair is unique. It replaces the immutable `GroupCatalogue` value when adding or
deleting a group, preserving insertion order. `ConfiguredGroups` supplies only the default five groups. `setGroups`
rejects a replacement catalogue that would leave an assignment pointing to a missing group, and `deleteGroup` rejects
an assigned group rather than cascading relationship deletion.

`ModelManager` exposes filtered Student and Guardian views for the UI while keeping the full `AddressBook` available for authoritative lookup and saving. The diagram omits the retired Person classes, which remain only for source compatibility.
`StorageManager` implements `Storage` and delegates register and user-preference file access to
`JsonAddressBookStorage` and `JsonUserPrefsStorage`, respectively. These collaborators are supplied through its
constructor. User preferences are stored separately from the student and guardian register.
`JsonAddressBookStorage` reads and writes JSON through `JsonUtil`. It creates a `JsonSerializableAddressBook`
from the complete `ReadOnlyAddressBook` when saving and calls `toModelType()` on the loaded wrapper when reading.
* `JsonAdaptedStudent` stores student IDs, names, academic levels and optional student phones.
* `JsonAdaptedGuardian` stores guardian IDs, names and phone numbers.
* `JsonAdaptedGroup` stores each group's canonical code, normalized label and Subject/Class kind.
* `JsonAdaptedGuardianLink` stores a student ID and guardian ID for each relationship.
* `JsonAdaptedGroupAssignment` stores a student ID and group code for each assignment.
The relationship adapters store IDs and codes rather than references to other adapters. Loading reconstructs the
catalogue before group assignments, so saved custom codes can be resolved, and reconstructs students and guardians
before validating assignment and guardian-link references. A conversion failure prevents a partially validated
register from being returned. For backward compatibility, an absent `groups` property uses `ConfiguredGroups`; an
explicit array, including an empty one, is saved and loaded as the authoritative catalogue.
When a register load fails, `StorageManager` retains the failure and blocks subsequent register saves for that
storage session. User-preference storage remains independent. Normal register writes are not atomic; the
in-memory rollback performed by Logic after a save failure does not guarantee restoration of disk contents.

This section describes some noteworthy details on how certain features are implemented.

The proposed undo/redo mechanism is facilitated by `VersionedAddressBook`. It extends `AddressBook` with an undo/redo history, stored internally as an `addressBookStateList` and `currentStatePointer`. Additionally, it implements the following operations:
* `VersionedAddressBook#commit()` — Saves the current address book state in its history.
* `VersionedAddressBook#undo()` — Restores the previous address book state from its history.
* `VersionedAddressBook#redo()` — Restores a previously undone address book state from its history.
These operations are exposed in the `Model` interface as `Model#commitAddressBook()`, `Model#undoAddressBook()` and `Model#redoAddressBook()` respectively.
Given below is an example usage scenario and how the undo/redo mechanism behaves at each step.

Step 1. The user launches the application for the first time. The `VersionedAddressBook` will be initialized with the initial address book state, and the `currentStatePointer` pointing to that single address book state.

Step 2. The user executes `delete 5` command to delete the 5th person in the address book. The `delete` command calls `Model#commitAddressBook()`, causing the modified state of the address book after the `delete 5` command executes to be saved in the `addressBookStateList`, and the `currentStatePointer` is shifted to the newly inserted address book state.

Step 3. The user executes `add n/David …​` to add a new person. The `add` command also calls `Model#commitAddressBook()`, causing another modified address book state to be saved into the `addressBookStateList`.

<div markdown="span" class="alert alert-info">:information_source: **Note:** If a command fails its execution, it will not call `Model#commitAddressBook()`, so the address book state will not be saved into the `addressBookStateList`.

Step 4. The user now decides that adding the person was a mistake, and decides to undo that action by executing the `undo` command. The `undo` command will call `Model#undoAddressBook()`, which will shift the `currentStatePointer` once to the left, pointing it to the previous address book state, and restores the address book to that state.

<div markdown="span" class="alert alert-info">:information_source: **Note:** If the `currentStatePointer` is at index 0, pointing to the initial AddressBook state, then there are no previous AddressBook states to restore. The `undo` command uses `Model#canUndoAddressBook()` to check if this is the case. If so, it will return an error to the user rather
than attempting to perform the undo.

Similarly, how an undo operation goes through the `Model` component is shown below:

The `redo` command does the opposite — it calls `Model#redoAddressBook()`, which shifts the `currentStatePointer` once to the right, pointing to the previously undone state, and restores the address book to that state.

<div markdown="span" class="alert alert-info">:information_source: **Note:** If the `currentStatePointer` is at index `addressBookStateList.size() - 1`, pointing to the latest address book state, then there are no undone AddressBook states to restore. The `redo` command uses `Model#canRedoAddressBook()` to check if this is the case. If so, it will return an error to the user rather than attempting to perform the redo.

Step 5. The user then decides to execute the command `list`. Commands that do not modify the address book, such as `list`, will usually not call `Model#commitAddressBook()`, `Model#undoAddressBook()` or `Model#redoAddressBook()`. Thus, the `addressBookStateList` remains unchanged.

Step 6. The user executes `clear`, which calls `Model#commitAddressBook()`. Since the `currentStatePointer` is not pointing at the end of the `addressBookStateList`, all address book states after the `currentStatePointer` will be purged. Reason: It no longer makes sense to redo the `add n/David …​` command. This is the behavior that most modern desktop applications follow.

1. **NFR01 — Platform independence:** Mentora should work on Windows, Linux, and macOS computers that have Java 25 installed.
2. **NFR02 — Portability:** Mentora should run without an installer and should be distributed as a single JAR file.

3. **NFR03 — Local single-user operation:** Mentora should support one coordinator operating one local data set at a time and should not require an account, Internet connection, remote server, or real-time collaboration service.
4. **NFR04 — Human-editable storage:** Mentora should store its persistent data locally in a human-editable text format such as JSON and should not require a database management system.

5. **NFR05 — Capacity and responsiveness:** With 200 student records and their associated guardian, enrolment, and group data, Mentora should complete a valid command within one second on a reference computer with a 2 GHz four-core processor, 8 GB of RAM, an SSD, and Java 25.
6. **NFR06 — Startup performance:** With the data volume specified in NFR05, Mentora should load the local data and become ready for commands within three seconds on the same reference computer.

7. **NFR07 — Data integrity:** A state-changing command should either be saved completely or leave both the in-memory and persisted data unchanged. Mentora should preserve an unreadable or invalid data file instead of overwriting it.
8. **NFR08 — Keyboard accessibility:** Every core record-management function should be usable through typed commands without requiring a mouse.

9. **NFR09 — Screen compatibility:** The GUI should work without resolution-related inconvenience at 1920×1080 or higher with 100% or 125% display scaling, and all functions should remain usable at 1280×720 or higher with 150% scaling.
10. **NFR10 — Deliverable size:** The distributed JAR or ZIP file should not exceed 100 MB and should not contain unnecessarily large assets or unused libraries.

This is the command contract for Mentora's first release: one Singapore tuition-centre coordinator, a local Java desktop application, and roughly 30-200 active records. It deliberately supports one guardian per student, while a guardian may be shared by many students.

Commands and prefixes are case-insensitive; the documented lower-case spelling is displayed in help. Prefixes may appear in any order, but every prefix may occur only once. Values may not be empty unless a command explicitly says otherwise. Unknown text, unknown prefixes, a missing required prefix, or a repeated prefix produces:

Leading and trailing spaces in any value are trimmed. Consecutive internal spaces in names and search queries are collapsed to one space. Therefore `Mei   Lin`, ` mei lin `, and `Mei Lin` are the same name for matching and duplicate checks. The application retains the casing supplied by the user for display, but compares names case-insensitively.

The application generates immutable identifiers (`S-0001`, `S-0002`, ... for students and `G-0001`, `G-0002`, ... for guardians). These IDs, not the current list position, are used in commands so that search results cannot cause an accidental update or deletion. An ID is an uppercase `S-` or `G-` followed by four or more digits; it is not user-editable.

`edit-guardian gid/GUARDIAN_ID p/PHONE` parses the guardian ID as stable text and validates the phone through the shared `GuardianPhone` value type. Unknown guardian IDs and malformed parameters use the command contract's specified errors.
- `EditGuardianCommand` resolves the guardian, checks phone uniqueness, and replaces that record with the same ID and name and the new phone. The success result reports the number of linked students.

- After each successful command, `MainWindow` refreshes the selected student details from the model, so an open linked profile displays the latest guardian phone.

Mentora helps coordinators of small private tuition centres in Singapore manage student and guardian contacts through typed commands. It is designed for one coordinator working locally with approximately 30–200 active and prospective secondary-school students.

Use Mentora to keep student details, subject or class assignments, and guardian contact information together. Siblings can share a guardian record, so one saved contact can appear in every linked student's profile.

> **Current MVP build:** Supported commands are `add-student`, `edit-student`, `delete-student`, `add-guardian`, `list-guardians`, `find-guardian`, `edit-guardian`, `link-guardian`, `unlink-guardian`, `view-student`, `find-student`, `filter-students`, `list-students`, `list-groups`, `add-group`, `delete-group`, `assign-group`, `unassign-group`, `help`, and `exit`. Student phone can be entered during creation or updated with `edit-student`; guardian phone remains a separate contact. Subject and class groups can be created, deleted when unused, assigned to students, removed from assignments, and displayed in profiles. Legacy Address Book commands are no longer accepted. Interface images are mockups, and example IDs and counts are illustrative. See the [MVP Release Notes](ReleaseNotes.md) for a concise shipped-feature summary.

The project currently targets Java `25`. Release packages will be distributed through the [Mentora project releases](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-T10-4/tp/releases). Use the package and launch instructions supplied with a release that supports the Mentora commands.

For the current source build, follow [Setting up and getting started](SettingUp.md). Its generated JAR is named `addressbook.jar` and can be launched from its folder with `java -jar addressbook.jar`. The supported commands are listed in the current-build note above.

The **command box** accepts typed commands: enter one command and press **Enter**. The **result panel** explains whether it succeeded or what needs correcting. The **main list** displays students, search results or configured groups. The **student profile** shows academic level, the student's own phone (or `Phone: none`), assignments, and the linked guardian's current name and independent phone number. The **status bar** reports local saving and loading.

Enter `add-student n/Mei Lin al/Sec 2 p/91234567` to create a student with an optional direct contact number; omit `p/` when none is recorded. The result shows the generated student ID, and the list selects the new record. Use that ID in `edit-student sid/STUDENT_ID al/Sec 3` to update the academic level or `edit-student sid/STUDENT_ID p/98765432` to add or replace the student's phone. Enter `list-groups` to browse the catalogue, then `assign-group sid/STUDENT_ID g/MAT` to assign a group. Use `add-guardian n/Anita Lim p/91234567` to create a separate guardian contact, then `link-guardian sid/STUDENT_ID gid/GUARDIAN_ID` to show that contact in the student's profile. Use `find-student n/Mei`, `list-students`, and `view-student sid/STUDENT_ID` to locate and select students. Use `delete-student sid/STUDENT_ID` to permanently remove a student by ID, `help` to open the help window, or `exit` to close Mentora.
Words in `UPPER_CASE` are placeholders: replace `NAME` with a name such as `Mei Lin`. Do not type the placeholder itself.
* Commands and prefixes are case-insensitive. Use the lowercase spellings shown in this guide for consistency.

* Prefixes identify fields: `n/` for a name or query, `al/` for academic level, `p/` for phone, `sid/` for student ID, `gid/` for guardian ID, `g/` for group code, `l/` for group label, and `k/` for group kind.
* Prefixed fields can appear in any order, but each prefix may appear only once. All fields shown outside square brackets are required and must contain a value.
* Unknown text, unknown prefixes, repeated prefixes, and missing required fields produce `Invalid command format. Use: FORMAT`, where `FORMAT` is the correct command syntax.
* `list-groups` and `list-guardians` reject extra text. `help` accepts at most one command name. The current `exit` command still ignores extra arguments; stricter handling remains planned behavior.
* Leading and trailing spaces in values are removed. Repeated spaces within names and search queries become one space. Name casing is retained for display but ignored for matching.

* Use permanent IDs such as `S-0007` and `G-0003`, **not list positions**. Searching or sorting does not change an ID. IDs are generated by Mentora and cannot be edited; they use uppercase `S-` or `G-` followed by at least four digits.
| Value | What you can enter | Examples |

| Name | 1–80 characters after spaces are normalized. Must start and end with a Unicode letter; only letters, spaces, apostrophes, hyphens, and periods between letters are allowed. | `Mei Lin`, `O'Connor`, `S. Kumar` |
| Academic level | `Sec 1` through `Sec 5`, or `IP 1` through `IP 6`, case-insensitive. | `Sec 2`, `ip 4` (displayed as `IP 4`) |

| Phone | Eight digits starting with `3`, `6`, `8`, or `9`, optionally preceded by `+65` and a single space. No hyphens, brackets, or extensions. | `91234567`, `+6591234567`, `+65 91234567` all display as `+65 91234567` |
| Student or guardian ID | An existing generated ID of the correct type. | `sid/S-0007`, `gid/G-0003` |

| Group code | For a new group, 2–20 ASCII letters, digits, or hyphens; starts with a letter and ends with a letter or digit. Existing-group commands require an exact code from `list-groups`. Codes are case-insensitive and display in uppercase. | `MAT`, `S2-MAT-A` |
| Group label | 1–80 characters after leading, trailing, and repeated internal whitespace are normalized. | `Physics`, `Secondary 3 Physics B` |
| Search query | 1–80 characters after spaces are normalized, following the name character rules. Can be a whole or partial name. | `mei`, `Mei Lin` |

Creates a student with a generated ID, no guardian, and no subject or class assignments. The list refreshes and selects the new student. If a search filter hides the new record, it is cleared after saving succeeds.
Example result: `Added student S-0007: Mei Lin (Sec 2).`
![Mockup of a newly added student with no assignments or guardian](mockup/add-student.png)
A student with the same normalized name and academic level is rejected with, for example, `A student named Mei Lin at Sec 2 already exists.` The same name at different levels is allowed.

The optional student phone uses the same Singapore number validation and canonical `+65 XXXXXXXX` display as a guardian phone. It is stored on the student record, is not required to be unique, and is separate from a linked guardian's number. Without a number the profile says `Phone: none`. Successful creation with a number reports `Added student S-0007: Mei Lin (Sec 2) with phone +65 91234567.`
**MVP limitation:** This rule also rejects two different students who share both their name and academic level. The MVP does not yet provide a way to distinguish them.

Changes the student's academic level, retaining the same ID, name, student phone, group assignments, and guardian link. The list and selected profile refresh, with a result such as `Updated student S-0007: academic level is now Sec 3.` Review class assignments separately when a student moves up a level.

Lookup and duplicate checks use every registered student, including records hidden by a search. After a successful edit, a filter hiding the target is cleared and that student is selected. The command keeps the current tab; select Students if Groups is open. Command and prefix names ignore case, either prefix order works, and each nonempty prefix is required exactly once.
If the change would duplicate another student's name and level, it is rejected: `Cannot update S-0007: a student named Mei Lin at Sec 3 already exists.` This command does not edit names.

To add or replace the student's own number, use `edit-student sid/S-0007 p/98765432`. Success reports `Updated student S-0007 phone to +65 98765432.` The number is validated by the shared Singapore phone rule, may be shared with other records, and does not change the guardian phone. An unknown ID reports `Student S-0007 does not exist.`; a save failure retains the old number and reports `Could not save changes. Student S-0007 was not updated.` The level and phone prefixes may also be supplied together to update both fields in one command.

Shows every registered student's ID, name and academic level, sorted by normalized name and then ID. Use it to return to the full list after a search. Guardian status is not displayed in this increment.
The result reports the number of students, for example `Listed 8 student(s).` If there are none, it says `No students registered.`
* `find-student n/mei` finds names containing `mei`, such as `Mei Lin` and `Mei Wen`.
* `find-student n/Mei Lin` finds names containing the phrase `Mei Lin`.

Matching ignores case and uses a substring of the normalized name, so partial names work. A multiword query is one phrase, not separate alternative keywords. This command does not search guardian names, academic levels, or assignments.
The main list shows all matches and reports, for example, `Found 2 student(s) matching "mei".` A valid query with no matches reports `No students match "mei".`
Search and list commands change only the displayed Student list and do not save data. They keep the current tab; select Students to see results if Groups is open.

* `filter-students g/MAT` shows students assigned to Mathematics.
* `filter-students al/Sec 2` shows students whose academic level is Sec 2.
Supply exactly one variant. Group codes and academic levels ignore case. Group filtering accepts configured
**Subject** groups such as `MAT`; Class groups such as `S2-MAT-A` are rejected. Academic-level filtering accepts
`Sec 1` through `Sec 5` or `IP 1` through `IP 6`, independently of group assignments.
Both variants open Students and show the active filter above the list. Each search replaces the previous student

ID. Select a row to open its profile. Run `list-students` to restore all students and clear the filter summary;
`find-student` also replaces the filter. Filtering never saves or changes stored records.
Example results are `Found 2 student(s) assigned to MAT.` and `Found 3 student(s) at Sec 2.` With no matches,

`Invalid command format. Use: filter-students g/GROUP_CODE` or

The two phone numbers are independent. If a search hides the student, the filter is cleared after successful lookup. The command keeps the current tab: select Students if Groups is open. It never saves data.
Use the ID shown in the student list or search results. To change information, use the relevant editing, linking, or assignment command.

**Deletion permanently removes the student record, that student's group assignments, and that student's guardian link.** Check the ID and profile before using this command. It is intended for records created by mistake, not for archiving withdrawn or graduated students.

Deleting the selected student clears the selection and profile. Deleting another student preserves the current selection. The search filter and active tab remain unchanged.

Example result: `Deleted student S-0007: Mei Lin.` If the student had a linked guardian, the result also says `Guardian link removed; guardian G-0003 was retained.` An unknown ID reports `Student S-0007 does not exist.` If saving fails, the complete register, filter, selection and workspace are restored, and the result says `Could not save changes. Student S-0007 was not deleted.`

Command and prefix names ignore case. Supply exactly one nonempty `sid/` value in uppercase `S-` form followed by at least four digits. Missing, repeated or unknown prefixes, malformed IDs and extra text report `Invalid command format. Use: delete-student sid/STUDENT_ID`.

Creates a guardian record and reports its ID, for example `Added guardian G-0003: Anita Lim (+65 91234567).` Guardians are saved independently. Browse them with `list-guardians` or search their names with `find-guardian`.

Phone numbers must be unique after normalization. If the number is already recorded, the result identifies the existing guardian: `A guardian with phone +65 91234567 already exists (G-0003). Link that guardian instead.` Different guardians may have the same name, but cannot have the same phone number in the MVP.

Switches to the Guardians tab, clears any guardian filter, and lists every guardian by normalized name and then guardian ID. Each row shows the guardian's ID, name, canonical phone number and linked-student count. Selecting a row shows the guardian profile and every linked student's ID and name.

The result is `Listed 6 guardian(s).`, using the actual number of guardian records. An empty register reports and displays `No guardians registered.` Command casing is ignored. Extra input reports `Invalid command format. Use: list-guardians` and leaves the current tab and list unchanged. Listing guardians is read-only and does not rewrite local data.

Switches to the Guardians tab and displays names containing the query, ignoring case and normalizing whitespace. A multiword query is matched as one phrase. Results are sorted by normalized name and then guardian ID. Guardians with the same name remain separate records. Phone numbers, IDs and linked student names are not searched.

Each row shows the contact details and linked-student count; selecting a row shows its linked students. The result reports, for example, `Found 2 guardian(s) matching "anita".` A search with no results shows an empty list and `No guardians match "anita".` Run `list-guardians` to clear the search.

Queries must contain 1-80 characters after whitespace normalization and follow the shared name rules. Invalid values report `Search query must be 1-80 characters and contain name characters only.` Missing or blank queries, repeated prefixes and additional parameters report `Invalid command format. Use: find-guardian n/QUERY`. Rejected searches preserve the current tab and list.
Guardian search does not alter student filters or stored records and remains available during storage recovery.

Updates the shared guardian's phone while retaining their ID, name, all student links and group assignments. Every linked student profile then shows the new number, including an affected profile that is already open. The current workspace and selected student are retained.

Command and prefix names are case-insensitive, and either prefix order is accepted. Supply exactly one nonempty `gid/` and `p/` value. Guardian IDs require uppercase `G-` followed by at least four ASCII digits. Missing, empty, repeated or unknown prefixes, malformed IDs and unexpected preamble report `Invalid command format. Use: edit-guardian gid/GUARDIAN_ID p/PHONE`.

Phones require eight digits starting with `3`, `6`, `8` or `9`, optionally prefixed by `+65` with zero or one following space. Leading/trailing spaces are removed. `98765432`, `+6598765432` and `+65 98765432` all display as `+65 98765432`. Invalid phone values report `Phone number must be an 8-digit Singapore number, optionally prefixed by +65.`
Example result: `Updated guardian G-0003 phone to +65 98765432. Updated contact will appear in 2 linked student profile(s).` The count depends on the guardian's links.

If another guardian already uses the normalized number, the update is rejected with, for example, `Phone +65 98765432 is already used by guardian G-0004.` An unknown ID reports `Guardian G-0003 does not exist.` Neither rejection changes the register.
Supplying the current phone number, including an equivalent local or `+65` form, reports the normal success message and linked-student count without rewriting the file.

Successful changes survive restarting Mentora. If saving fails, the previous in-memory register and phone are restored and the result says `Could not save changes. Guardian G-0003 was not updated.`, using the supplied ID. This command is blocked during load recovery, even when the supplied phone is unchanged. See [Saving and reopening](#saving-and-reopening) for recovery instructions and the normal-save limitation.

Example result: `Linked student S-0007 (Mei Lin) to guardian G-0003 (Anita Lim, +65 91234567).`

Repeating a link reports `Student S-0007 is already linked to guardian G-0003.` Trying to link a different guardian while a link exists reports `Student S-0007 already has guardian G-0003. Unlink it before linking another guardian.`

Removes the relationship while keeping both records and the guardian's links to other students. The profile shows `Guardian: none`.
Example result: `Removed guardian G-0003 from student S-0007. Guardian record was retained.` If there is no existing link, it reports `Student S-0007 has no guardian to unlink.`

Permanently removes one existing group without deleting students or guardians. To prevent accidental assignment loss, Mentora deletes only groups with no assigned students. Use `unassign-group` for each student before deleting an assigned group.

Example result: `Deleted group S3-PHY-B: Secondary 3 Physics B (Class).` After saving succeeds, Mentora opens the Groups tab and refreshes the catalogue. The deleted code is no longer available to assignment or filtering commands.

Missing, empty, repeated, or unknown parameters report `Invalid command format. Use: delete-group g/GROUP_CODE`.

If saving fails, the group is restored and the result says `Could not save changes. Group S3-PHY-B was not deleted.` Successful deletion is permanent and has no undo command. Group deletion is unavailable during storage recovery.

Example result: `Assigned group S2-MAT-A (Secondary 2 Mathematics A) to student S-0007.` The application opens Students, selects the target and refreshes Assignments, including when that student was already selected. A search filter hiding the target is cleared only after saving succeeds. Selecting another student shows their assignments. Scroll the profile when a long name or several assignments exceed the available space; an unassigned student shows `No groups assigned.`

Command and prefix names are case-insensitive, and either prefix order is accepted. Student IDs must retain their uppercase `S-` form with at least four digits. Each prefix is required exactly once, with one nonempty ID/code value. Missing, repeated or unknown prefixes and extra text report `Invalid command format. Use: assign-group sid/STUDENT_ID g/GROUP_CODE`.

An unknown student reports `Student S-0007 does not exist.` Group-code comparisons ignore case and feedback uses the canonical uppercase code. Removes exactly one existing assignment, including a student's final assignment. This does not delete the student: their ID, name, academic level and guardian link remain unchanged, as do all guardian records, other assignments, other students and the configured group catalogue.

Example result: `Removed group S2-MAT-A from student S-0007.` After saving succeeds, Mentora opens Students, selects the target and refreshes the profile, including when that student was already selected. Removing the final assignment shows `No groups assigned.` Switching students or workspaces continues to show the current assignments.
The command finds students in the complete register. If a search hides the target, its filter is cleared only after saving succeeds; a filter that already includes the target is retained.

Command and prefix names are case-insensitive, and either prefix order is accepted. Supply exactly one nonempty `sid/` and `g/` value. Student IDs require uppercase `S-` followed by at least four ASCII digits (`0`–`9`). Missing, repeated or unknown prefixes, malformed IDs, empty values and extra text report `Invalid command format. Use: unassign-group sid/STUDENT_ID g/GROUP_CODE`. Group codes are case-insensitive and feedback uses their canonical uppercase form.

An unknown student reports `Student S-0007 does not exist.` An unavailable group reports `Group CODE is not configured. Run list-groups to see available groups.` If the configured group is not assigned to the student, the result is `Student S-0007 is not assigned to S2-MAT-A.`

If saving fails, the in-memory removal is rolled back and the result says `Could not save changes. The group assignment was not removed.` Syntactically valid removals are blocked during load recovery. See [Saving and reopening](#saving-and-reopening) for recovery instructions and the normal-save limitation.
When a student changes class, remove their old class assignment and assign the new class using its configured code.
Enter `help` to open or bring forward the command overview. The result says `Opened help window.`
Enter `help add-student`, for example, to display that command's syntax, examples, validation rules and common
errors. The result says `Showing help for add-student.` Command names ignore case. A new request updates the
same help window, and `help` or the Help menu/F1 returns it to the overview.
Help content is bundled with Mentora and works offline, including during storage recovery. The copy button
copies the URL of this Mentora User Guide; opening the online guide requires an internet connection.
An unknown name reports `No help is available for "COMMAND". Run help to see all commands.` More than one
argument reports `Invalid command format. Use: help [COMMAND]`. Rejected requests keep the previous help page.

The current build saves the complete Student, Guardian, group-catalogue, guardian-link, and assignment register after successful changes from `add-student`, `edit-student`, `delete-student`, `add-guardian`, `edit-guardian`, `link-guardian`, `unlink-guardian`, `add-group`, `delete-group`, `assign-group`, and `unassign-group`. Editing to the existing academic level or the guardian's existing phone number does not rewrite the file. Viewing, searching, listing, help, and exit do not rewrite data. Saving while filtered retains every registered student. There is no manual save command, account, or network connection required. The file is `data/addressbook.json` relative to the folder from which you launched Mentora; its location appears in the status bar.

When Mentora reopens, it loads the complete register. Older files without guardians, guardian links, or assignments load with those collections empty; an older file without a `groups` property receives the five default groups. **Can siblings share a guardian?** Yes. Add the guardian once and link each student to the same guardian ID. The current guardian name and phone are shown in every linked student's profile. Use `edit-guardian` to update that shared phone number for every linked student.
**Does deleting a student delete their guardian?** No. It removes that student and their relationship, preserving the guardian and other students' links.

**Does changing academic level move the student to a new class?** No. Academic level and group assignments are independent. Use `unassign-group` to remove the old assignment and `assign-group` to add the new class.
**Why can I not delete a group?** Mentora prevents deletion while any student is assigned to the group. Remove each assignment with `unassign-group`, then run `delete-group` again.
**Can I keep a withdrawn student's record without showing it in the main list?** Archiving and active-only lists are deferred. Deletion is permanent and is not an archive operation.
**Can two guardians use the same number?** The MVP treats the normalized phone number as unique, so separate guardian records cannot share a number.

Mentora is a desktop application for managing contact details. It provides a graphical interface and a command line interface for working with contacts. The user interacts with it using a CLI, and it has a GUI created with JavaFX. It is written in Java, and has about 10 kLoC.
Given below are my contributions to the project.
* **New Feature**: Added the ability to undo/redo previous commands.
* What it does: allows the user to undo all previous commands one at a time. Preceding undo commands can be reversed by using the redo command.
* Justification: This feature improves the product significantly because a user can make mistakes in commands and the app should provide a convenient way to rectify them.

* Highlights: This enhancement affects existing commands and commands to be added in future. It required an in-depth analysis of design alternatives. The implementation too was challenging as it required changes to existing commands.
